lesson.lesson_summary: Learners already know the -self words as reflexive pronouns (1-3-5). This lesson shows the same words used for emphasis: placed right after a noun or at the end of the clause, they stress who did something. Learners use the removal test to tell an emphatic pronoun from a reflexive one.

success_criteria: Find an emphatic pronoun after a noun or at the end of a clause.
Add one to stress who did something.

learning_objectives.description: Tell emphatic pronouns from reflexive pronouns.

pages.title: Adding Extra Force

content.text: The -self words can also add emphasis. They stress that this person, and nobody else, did something.

examples.sentence: The chef himself carried out our dessert.
examples.explanation: Himself stresses that the chef, not a waiter, brought the dessert.

pages.key_takeaway: An emphatic pronoun stresses who did it.

pages.title: Right After the Noun

content.text: An emphatic pronoun often sits right after the noun it stresses.

examples.sentence: The mayor herself opened the new library.
examples.explanation: Herself follows the mayor and stresses that she came in person.

examples.sentence: The walls themselves were made of mud.
examples.explanation: Themselves stresses the walls, not just the roof or floor.

pages.key_takeaway: Place it right after the noun to stress that noun.

pages.title: At the End of the Clause

content.text: An emphatic pronoun can also come at the end, after the whole action.

examples.sentence: I baked this lemon cake myself.
examples.explanation: Myself at the end stresses that nobody helped.

examples.sentence: You can fix the puncture yourself.
examples.explanation: Yourself stresses that you don't need a mechanic.

pages.key_takeaway: It can also stand at the end for emphasis.

pages.title: Same Word, Different Use

items.label: Reflexive
items.description: The doer is also the receiver.

items.label: Emphatic
items.example: Tara herself taught the guitar class.

comparison_points: Without herself, the first sentence loses its meaning.
Without herself, the second still makes sense.
content.conclusion: A reflexive pronoun is needed; an emphatic one only adds force.

pages.key_takeaway: Reflexive is needed; emphatic adds force.

pages.title: The Removal Test

content.rule_text: Take the -self word out. If the sentence still makes sense, it was emphatic. If the sentence breaks, it was reflexive.
content.scope: Myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves

examples.sentence: The children themselves chose the song.
examples.explanation: 'The children chose the song' still works, so themselves is emphatic.

pages.key_takeaway: Remove it: still fine means emphatic.

pages.title: Emphatic Pronouns: Recap

items: Emphatic pronouns stress who did something.
They come right after the noun or at the end.
They look just like reflexive pronouns.
Remove the word: if the sentence still works, it was emphatic.

pages.key_takeaway: Use a -self word to say 'this one and no other'.

question_bank.prompt: Identify the emphatic pronoun in: 'The principal herself handed out the prizes.'
question_bank.explanation: Herself follows the principal and stresses that she gave the prizes in person.

question_bank.prompt: Where can an emphatic pronoun go?

options.text: Right after the noun, or at the end of the clause
Only at the very start of a sentence

question_bank.explanation: Emphatic pronouns sit right after the noun they stress, or at the end of the clause.

question_bank.prompt: Complete for emphasis: 'We made all the paper lanterns ___.'
question_bank.explanation: The subject is we, so ourselves stresses that we made them with no help.

question_bank.prompt: In which sentence is the -self word emphatic?

options.text: The king himself welcomed the guests.
The king hurt himself on the stairs.
The king saw himself in the mirror.

question_bank.explanation: 'The king welcomed the guests' still works, so himself is emphatic there. In the others, removing it breaks the sentence.

question_bank.prompt: In 'Arun dried himself with a towel', himself is emphatic.
question_bank.explanation: 'Arun dried with a towel' doesn't work, so himself is reflexive: Arun dried Arun.

question_bank.prompt: Identify the emphatic pronoun in: 'The pilot himself spoke to the passengers.'
question_bank.explanation: Himself stresses that the pilot, not a crew member, spoke.

question_bank.prompt: What does myself add in 'I planted these roses myself'?

options.text: It stresses that I did it, not someone else.
It shows that I hurt myself.
It shows that the roses planted themselves.

question_bank.explanation: Myself at the end adds emphasis: the speaker did the planting personally.

question_bank.prompt: Which sentence has a reflexive, not an emphatic, pronoun?
question_bank.explanation: 'Mira taught to swim' breaks, so herself is reflexive there. The other two still work without it.

question_bank.prompt: Complete for emphasis: 'The singer ___ signed my ticket.'
question_bank.explanation: Himself or herself after the singer stresses that the singer signed it personally.

question_bank.prompt: If you remove an emphatic pronoun, the sentence still makes sense.
question_bank.explanation: An emphatic pronoun only adds force, so the sentence works without it.

cross_references.reason: Taught in 1-3-5; contrasted here on one page.

cross_references.concept: Mistakes such as hisself and 'Call Anita or myself'
